verdict.statement: All three RT21 blocking findings are genuinely repaired under reviewer-constructed falsifiers that were never replayed from author fixtures. The actual production return is the frozen V3 mappingproxy with the eight ordered fields ending in hostApiBinding; the reviewer independently recomputed the committed checker-source SHA-256 and all seven implementation AST digests, proved each digest is sensitive only to its own implementation body, and observed each of the seven wrappers authenticate before, route exactly once to, and pass through unchanged the result of its declared implementation. The inert authenticator refuses composite alias, integer range, byte budget, forbidden identity, malformed registry/forbidden-map/budget, and every exotic Python kind with named findings and zero exception escapes, while correctly admitting the legal seven kinds and the canonical empty-tuple and scalar reuse exceptions. The active checker source contains zero snapshot.operations consumers of any form. Trust order, the 55-pin closed read set, the D9 v1.13 live derivation, the capability closure, the lease protocol, and purge/ProjectId lineage were each recomputed independently and are correct. Three non-blocking findings are recorded; none of them, alone or together, defeats a claimed property.

newFindings.finding: hostApiBinding.checkerSourceSha256 and all seven implementationAstSha256 rows are computed from pathlib.Path(__file__).read_bytes() at main() time. Nothing binds those digests to the code objects that are actually executing. The reviewer ran the genuine 497909c2... bytes in a process whose __file__ held different bytes; the checker exited 0 and committed checkerSourceSha256 = f25a8777..., a digest for source that never executed. The interpreter compiles the script at startup and main() re-reads it afterwards, so the two byte sequences are only assumed equal. The 55 pinned predecessors do NOT have this gap - PROBE-A shows every predecessor compile carries the exact pinned digest - it is confined to the checker's own source.
newFindings.reproducibleCondition: Execute the exact RT22 checker bytes with __file__ pointing at a path whose on-disk content differs (probe_f_gap.py case F2). Run exits 0; binding commits the on-disk digest.
newFindings.whyNotBlocking: RT22 does not claim this property: the constructor signature names its third parameter CapturedCheckerSourceV1, returnedSnapshot.retainsExactly says 'the captured checker source SHA-256', and verifierTcb scopes its sourceExecutionOrder guarantee to the 55 local buffers. No checker can bootstrap trust in its own executing bytes, and an adversary able to write the checker file already controls the verifier entirely.
requiredRepair: Disclose the residual explicitly in retentionResiduals: hostApiBinding attests the captured on-disk source, not the executing code objects.

Optionally strengthen integrity-of-record by additionally committing a digest over the LIVE __code__ (co_code plus normalized co_consts) of each of the seven implementations and refusing when it disagrees with the AST-derived row; this closes accidental drift and the 'honest execution, swapped attestation file' case, though not the fully compromised-verifier case.

newFindings.finding: mustNotRetain forbids 'any ... mutable mapping'. In CPython, gc.get_referents(mappingproxy) yields the live mutable backing dict, and the reviewer mutated the returned snapshot through it. The claim is exact along the contract's own declared semantic-child denominator (mapping value and tuple item), where PROBE-C6 confirms a plain dict is refused as RT22-INERT-FORBIDDEN-KIND:builtins.dict; it is not exact along the raw CPython referent graph.
newFindings.whyNotBlocking: The architecture does not rely on Python-level immutability. Every mutation the reviewer performed - kind change, extra key, deep nested change - was caught on re-authentication as RT22-SNAPSHOT-KIND, RT22-SNAPSHOT-FIELDS or RT22-SNAPSHOT-COMMITMENT, and every one of the seven host wrappers refused the tampered snapshot with AuthorityError before touching its implementation. The guarantee that carries is commitment re-authentication at each entry point, and it holds.
requiredRepair: Disclosure only: state that deep immutability is enforced by V3 commitment re-authentication at every host entry point rather than by MappingProxyType alone, and scope mustNotRetain to the declared semantic-child denominator.

scopeLimitationsAndResiduals: This review covers exactly the four frozen inputs plus the transitive pinned set the checker reads. evaluation-proof.v8 was treated as a passed frozen root and was NOT re-reviewed.
All probes ran on CPython 3.14.6 / darwin arm64 under python3 -I -B. Behaviour on other interpreters or platforms is unexercised.

Most probe runs in this review were performed in a disposable tree at /private/tmp/rt22-indep-reviewer-sb, because a coordinator-induced transient had drifted one pinned dependency in the repository (see workspaceMutations). After restoration the repository normal and --selftest runs were repeated and their stdout is byte-identical to the disposable-tree runs, so the disposable-tree evidence is authoritative for the repository state. No repository byte was written by this reviewer other than this artifact.

An independent Consumer-B implementer litmus returned LITMUS-FAIL during this review window. The coordinator states its blocking escalations concerned neither V10 nor retention custody. This reviewer did NOT read, verify, or use that artifact as evidence; it is outside the four frozen subjects and had no influence on this verdict, in either direction.

PROBE-E8 shows a pinned dependency may be a symlink to identical bytes outside the tree and still pass. The checker binds bytes and (dev, ino, size, mtime_ns) identity, not location. This is consistent with its stated contract and is recorded as a boundary, not a defect.
The negative purge fixtures PN-01..PN-04 declare invariants without expected outputs, so the reviewer could not recompute them; only the three positive fixtures were independently reproduced.
No production byte store, liveness, fencing, persistence, transaction, durability, recovery, crash, concurrency, or atomicity implementation is demonstrated by RT22 and none was reviewed.
This review makes no statement about any concurrently reviewed artifact, including evidence.v8.

Reviewer byproducts, all outside the repository: /private/tmp/rt22-indep-reviewer-sb/ (disposable tree, probe scripts, per-case tamper trees) and /tmp/rt22n{1,2,3}.txt, /tmp/rt22s{1,2,3}.txt, /tmp/rt22emit.json, /tmp/rt22emit.err (determinism capture). No __pycache__ was created anywhere.
